summary: Comprehensive SUP-0/1/2/3 backend + frontend testing for the new in-house Wayly Support Ticketing system. 16 of 17 pytest cases pass (1 skipped due to unrelated signup form selector). Frontend report-an-issue flow from Statement Decoder to /support inbox is fully functional. SUPPORT_TRIAGE_ENABLED=false gate confirmed clean (zero sup_triage rows, zero 'triage call failed' log entries). One backend bug found and fixed during testing: Pydantic body models declared inside the build_support_router() closure were being mis-typed as query params by FastAPI, returning 422 on /status, /defects (create), /link-defect, /defects/{id}/resolve and /triage/agree. Moved all body models to module scope to fix.

minor.issue: Fresh signup attempt during fixture returned non-200 (likely required fields not in JSON payload — test fixture issue, not a SUP-* bug). Caused the User A vs User B isolation test to skip. Recommend re-running with a known-good signup payload.

action_items: Backend fix already applied: Pydantic body models (StatusBody, DefectCreate, DefectLink, DefectResolve, TriageAgree) moved from inside build_support_router() to module level in /app/backend/routes/support.py. This unblocked the 422 errors. Please review/keep.

Optional: harden the user-vs-user list isolation test by aligning the signup payload (currently failing the signup step in the fixture). The actual route filtering by user_id is verified indirectly via DB inspection.
critical_code_review_comments: Pydantic body model placement: inner closure classes confuse FastAPI body detection — keep these at module scope (now fixed).
_strip helper mutates the passed dict in place; harmless here, but consider returning a copy for safety.

_run_triage stores 'needs_human' triage row on LLM exception even when the flag is off path early-returns first; behaviour is correct, but consider counting failures separately so the absence-of-triage invariant when flag=false is observable in metrics.

Admin admin_list_tickets sort is ('status', 1), ('created_at', 1) — alphabetical sort on status puts 'awaiting_user' before 'received' which is fine for the demo but for a real 'oldest unresolved first' ordering consider a $expr/aggregation that explicitly excludes resolved/closed from the top of the queue.
purge_expired_attachments helper exists but is not scheduled — needs a cron/scheduler hook for the 90-day retention guarantee to be honoured in production.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend SUP-* router is fully working after the Pydantic body fix. Triage flag stays OFF — do NOT enable SUPPORT_TRIAGE_ENABLED unless the user explicitly asks. Frontend Report-an-Issue flow on Statement Decoder verified end-to-end (panel opens, 5 cats render, submit produces WAY-XXXX, navigates to /support, list + detail render). My Support sidebar link works. Empty-state test on a fresh user was not fully run because the signup form selector in this app uses non-standard input names — to test, sign up via the UI manually or via /api/auth/signup with full payload (name, email, password, plan).
rca of the issue: Pydantic body classes (StatusBody, DefectCreate, DefectLink, DefectResolve, TriageAgree) were declared INSIDE build_support_router(). FastAPI evaluates parameter type annotations at decoration time; when a closure-scoped class is annotated as `body: StatusBody`, the body-vs-query inference in FastAPI failed (returning {loc: ['query', 'body'], msg: 'Field required'}) on 5 admin endpoints. Repro: POST /api/admin/support/tickets/{id}/status with valid JSON → 422. Fix: moved the 5 inner Pydantic models to module scope. Verified by re-running pytest — all 5 endpoints now return 200.
